verdict_text:
YES

The script builds the keep index per head-bearing tensor exactly as required: for the fused `c_attn.weight` and `c_attn.bias` it keeps the 64-wide blocks of heads 0..4 and 6..11 within each of the three 768-wide segments, producing columns/rows 0..319, 384..767, 768..1087, 1152..1535, 1536..1855, 1920..2303 in order (clauses 1 and 2). For `c_proj.weight` it keeps rows 0..319 and 384..767 (clause 3). All other tensors are left untouched with unchanged names (clause 4), and the output is a single file with 160 tensors (clause 5). All four required checks are asserted before `save_file`, so the script fails loudly before writing if any does not hold. The only external dependency is a `_ckpt.load_checkpoint` helper, assumed to load the safetensors file into a plain state dict.
